news.articleText: TÜİK açıkladı: Tarım-ÜFE ekimde yıllık yüzde 9,69 arttı - Tarım-ÜFE, ekimde aylık yüzde 1,02, yıllık yüzde 9,69 arttı. Yıllık ve aylık bazda en yüksek fiyat düşüşü ise turunçgillerde kaydedildi. Tarım ürünleri üretici fiyat endeksi (Tarım-ÜFE), ekim ayında bir önceki aya göre yüzde 1,02, geçen yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 9,69 yükseldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu (TÜİK), Ekim 2026 dönemine ilişkin Tarım-ÜFE verilerini açıkladı. Buna göre Tarım-ÜFE, ekimde bir önceki aya kıyasla yüzde 1,02, geçen yılın aralık ayına göre yüzde 8,12, geçen yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 9,69 ve 12 aylık ortalamalara göre yüzde 27,64 arttı. Sektörler incelendiğinde, ekimde bir önceki aya göre tarım ve avcılık ürünleri ile ilgili hizmetlerde yüzde 1,13 artış kaydedildi. Ormancılık ürünleri ve ilgili hizmetlerde yüzde 0,37, balık ve diğer balıkçılık ürünleri ile su ürünlerinde yüzde 0,75 azalış gerçekleşti. Ana gruplarda ise tek yıllık bitkisel ürünlerde yüzde 7,94, canlı hayvanlar ve hayvansal ürünlerde yüzde 0,91 artış görülürken çok yıllık bitkisel ürünlerde yüzde 7,13 düşüş kaydedildi. Yıllık ve aylık değişimde turunçgiller öne çıktı Yıllık değişimin en yüksek olduğu alt grup, yüzde 57,83 azalışla turunçgiller oldu. Aylık bazda da en yüksek düşüş yüzde 27,67 ile yine turunçgillerde gerçekleşti.

news.title: Ex-Robinhood engineer pleads guilty to $125K Hyperliquid trading scheme
news.summary: The former Robinhood engineer used confidential information about upcoming Robinhood token listings to trade on Hyperliquid.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Ex-Robinhood engineer pleads guilty to $125K Hyperliquid trading scheme
news.summaryTr: The former Robinhood engineer used confidential information about upcoming Robinhood token listings to trade on Hyperliquid.
news.articleText: Ex-Robinhood engineer pleads guilty to $125K Hyperliquid trading scheme The former Robinhood engineer used confidential information about upcoming Robinhood token listings to trade on Hyperliquid. Former Robinhood software engineer Huaisong “Jerry” Xiang has pleaded guilty to wire fraud after using confidential information about upcoming crypto listings on the platform to trade perpetual futures on the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, earning $125,523 in illicit profits. On Monday, the US Department of Justice said that Xiang entered the plea before US District Judge Colleen McMahon and agreed to forfeit $125,523. Xiang faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison and is scheduled to be sentenced on Feb. 25, 2027. Prosecutors said the software engineer had access to nonpublic information about which tokens Robinhood Crypto planned to list and when. Between 2025 and 2026, he repeatedly bought perpetual futures tied to those tokens before the announcements were made public. The plea follows September charges against Xiang and another former Robinhood engineer, Hefu Chai. Both were accused of exploiting internal listing information to trade on Hyperliquid, with prosecutors initially alleging that each made over $50,000. The DOJ’s Monday announcement did not provide an update on Chai’s case. In May, crypto analytics firm Kaiko flagged suspicious Hyperliquid trading ahead of Robinhood’s Jan. 15 listing of Lighter (LIT). One of the wallets identified in its investigation matches an address that prosecutors later linked to Chai, who allegedly used it to trade LIT perpetuals ahead of the listing. Related: Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’

news.title: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72
news.summary: Efforts to recover bodies after a “double-tap” attack in southern Ukraine are being hampered by continuing Russian strikes, officials say.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72
news.summaryTr: Efforts to recover bodies after a “double-tap” attack in southern Ukraine are being hampered by continuing Russian strikes, officials say.
news.articleText: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72 - Published Ukrainian officials have accused Russia of targeting rescue and recovery operations two weeks after a deadly "double-tap" strike at a village close to the front line killed at least 72 people. Ukraine says Russia carried out two attacks in succession on a humanitarian aid centre in the village of Komyshuvakha on 2 November - including the use of what it said was a 3,000kg (6,600lb) aerial bomb on a shelter where residents had fled for safety. Verified images posted in the days after the attack show damage to emergency vehicles and excavation equipment at the site. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) told BBC Verify there have been multiple Russian strikes during the rescue. The DSNS said three police officers, four workers and two rescue dogs were injured while five vehicles were damaged. "Due to the threat of repeated shelling, emergency workers are constantly forced to periodically suspend work and retreat to a safe place," it added. The DSNS said the death toll had risen to at least 72 people making it one of the deadliest single incidents since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Oleksiy, an intelligence officer investigating the incident for Ukraine's SBU security service, who asked to be identified only by his first name, said rescue vehicles were "clearly marked" and accused Russia of "deliberately destroying humanitarian equipment". He added the village's infrastructure and the people still living in Komyshuvakha are also being systematically targeted by drones and bombs. Oleksiy accused Russian forces of "outright terror against civilians, against peaceful residents" to make life on the front line impossible. BBC Verify has confirmed videos being shared by Ukrainian police that show rescue workers at the scene shouting "drone, drone" and running for cover on the day after the 2 November attack. A group can also be seen treating a victim. Bodies are still to be recovered from the rubble, Oleksiy said. "The enemy knows perfectly well that what is being carried out there is essentially a humanitarian operation to search for the dead." BBC Verify has asked the Russian Ministry of Defence for comment specifically about the Komyshuvakha attacks but has not received a response. A general statement released on 2 November by the Russian MoD said it had targeted energy and transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian military across the country. While there are no military or industrial facilities in Komyshuvakha it is close to a key route used for Ukrainian troop movements, supplies and evacuations. The village was previously reported to have been struck by the Russians on 28 October. Fears of second strike heard on police radios Local people headed to the shelter area on 2 November after being told by a local Telegram group that aid would be distributed between 10:00 and 12:00 local time (08:00-10:00 GMT). Ukrainian authorities said an initial strike, at 09:45 local time, hit buildings above ground killing one woman. Bodycam footage, released by Ukrainian police in edited segments and analysed by BBC Verify, shows people trying to free a casualty from the rubble before declaring she had died. Throughout the footage, warnings of an impending second strike can be heard on police radios with increasing urgency until people are instructed to run to the underground shelter. The same footage, which was taken around an hour after the first attack, goes on to show people in a shelter. As they wait in silence a large explosion can be heard and the video goes dark. Aftermath video filmed later shows bodies being recovered from a large crater immediately above the shelter. Twisted iron and rubble from the structure below can be seen beneath the surface. Funerals have been held almost daily for the victims of the attack, including locals working to administer aid distribution, those seeking to collect it and soldiers who officials say arrived to assist with rescue efforts. Trevor Ball, bomb disposal expert at intelligence firm at Armament Research Services, said a crater seen in the footage was consistent with the damage and depth left by a FAB-3000, a 3,000kg Russian bomb which can destroy underground structures. His comments were echoed by Chris Proops, an ex-UK National Crime Agency investigator, who said the scale of the damage at the scene matched the size of the FAB-3000. Ball and Proops both confirmed verified photos of munition fragments obtained by BBC Verify from Ukrainian authorities show part of a guidance kit that is compatible with the FAB-3000, which increases the weapon's accuracy and allows it to be fired from a greater distance from the target. International law experts told BBC Verify that Russia had committed a war crime if it knowingly attacked rescue workers. Ben Saul, professor of international law at the University of Sydney, said this "appears to be either a deliberate attack on civilians or civilian objects - a war crime - or an indiscriminate attack - also a war crime". Prof Samuel Moyn of Yale University said "directly targeting rescuers or their equipment is a gross violation of international humanitarian law". Precautions have to be taken to ensure that strikes target combatants rather than others, he added. Additional reporting by Margaryta Maliukova, BBC Monitoring

news.summary: The US vice-president tells Fox News that when he makes a decision to run or otherwise, he will "be all in on whatever that decision is".

news.titleTr: Vance says he will decide 'sometime next year' about 2028 US presidential run
news.summaryTr: The US vice-president tells Fox News that when he makes a decision to run or otherwise, he will "be all in on whatever that decision is".
news.articleText: Vance says he will decide 'sometime next year' about 2028 US presidential run - Published US Vice-President JD Vance has said he will make a decision "sometime next year" about whether or not he will run for president in 2028. In an interview with Fox News, Vance would not provide a timeline on making a determination, but signaled he is not in a hurry to make up his mind. "I haven't made a decision. We'll figure it out sometime next year," Vance said. When pressed by host Laura Ingraham, he added: "When I make a decision, I'll be all in on whatever that decision is." The comments came amid growing interest in Vance's next moves in the weeks since voters handed both President Donald Trump and Republicans a resounding defeat in the midterm elections. People in Vance's orbit who have spoken to the BBC said the November elections did not change the timeline around his decision-making process for 2028. He is expected to run but allies believe he could wait several months to make a final decision. Speculation about Vance's White House aspirations began the moment President Trump selected him as his 2024 running mate. The pick positioned Vance, who entered the White House as one of the youngest vice-presidents in US history, as the most likely heir to Trump's Make America Great Again (Maga) movement. But while serving in office, Vance has carefully avoided discussing his own political ambitions. He kept that up during the midterms, when supporters frequently interrupted his campaign speeches to urge him to run in 2028. Vance's stock response was that Republicans needed to focus on the election at hand in November. But with the midterms in the rearview mirror, and Republicans eager to move on from their 2026 drubbing, the next election at hand is now the 2028 presidential race. - Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war - Published5 November - The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now? - Published8 November Vance would likely jump to the top of the Republican primary field whenever he launches his bid, should he choose to run. But the contest is expected to be a competitive process with a large field of candidates. Numerous other high-profile Republicans are rumoured to be interested in running or have said publicly that they are mulling a White House bid. The list includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, outgoing Florida Governor and 2024 hopeful Ron DeSantis, and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie, among others. Trump has praised Vance and Rubio on several occasions, while also insisting that he is not sure who he will endorse in 2028 - or if he will weigh in at all. The president's endorsement would be influential with the Maga base. But the midterms revealed widespread frustration with many of his second-term policies, complicating the path forward for potential candidates like Vance who are tied to Trump's agenda. Vance blamed the midterm results on the war with Iran in a post-election social media post. In it, he also mapped out a plan for winning back Republican voters, which included ending the war and focusing on the economy. The message was widely seen as a first step by Vance to distance himself from Trump ahead of a 2028 run. In the Fox News interview, Vance reiterated his view that the war came with a "political cost", but said it has not damaged his relationship with Trump. "There's no daylight" on the Iran war between Trump and senior administration officials including himself, Vance said. He added that Trump would not let the conflict become a "forever war" and said the administration would not let the war, which was launched by the US and Israel in February 2026, even become "a two-year commitment". Vance also discussed the nationwide air traffic outrage last week, which brought air travel across the US to a standstill for several hours. The vice-president called on lawmakers to fix the issue in the final weeks of the current congressional session. He also touched on the scandal engulfing Nvidia, its former CEO Jensen Huang and its implications for US-China relations. Vance said there was still no "clarity" about the accuracy of reports that a woman with whom Huang reportedly had an affair with was indeed a Chinese spy. "There is a lack of clarity about it. I don't know and [Trump] doesn't know whether this woman was a spy or not," Vance said. Related topics - Published6 November - Published7 November - Published4 November

news.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss
news.summary: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss
news.summaryTr: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
news.articleText: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss - Published Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for the company's co-founder Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, supported the effort. Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, joining a list of supporters including SpaceX's Elon Musk who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign. But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in reinstating him after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy. The same day, the White House also said it will further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia. The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. Since Huang's departure, more than 175,000 people have signed an open letter calling for the board to reinstate the tech billionaire while an ongoing internal probe is conducted. Major tech bosses, including Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return. The "Stand with Jensen" campaign claims to have been launched by current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, all demanding the return of the former chief executive. They expressed concerns the firm's co-founder "was removed without meaningful due process". Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back. Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of the affair but resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him. The scandal-hit tech boss was discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times, external, though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him. A representative for Huang declined to comment on the report. The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House. Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal erupted, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy". Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company. The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions. New rules The Trump administration on Monday also issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres, which have been allegedly used as a way for Chinese firms to gain access to advanced chips to train AI models. The move comes ahead of a meeting this week between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, whose countries are locked in a race to lead AI development. The interim rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to prevent them from being illegally diverted to China. The measure is designed to ensure existing restrictions on sensitive US technology "cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the Department of Commerce said. Huang has been a vocal advocate for easing chip export restrictions on China, arguing that broad access to global markets is crucial for the competitiveness of the US. He said in 2025 that the market for AI chips in China would eventually reach $50bn - a sum Huang said "is like Boeing - not a plane - the entire company". In 2025, Nvidia won an approval to sell some advanced AI chips in China after Huang's repeated lobbying efforts in Washington. - How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security? - Published4 days ago - How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House - Published3 days ago The ex-Nvidia boss' affair with Alice Huang, the former director of a Singaporean data centre firm called Megaspeed, has raised the level of scrutiny over deals abroad. The small South East Asian business hub has been a draw for companies all around the world, many of which have set up headquarters in Singapore. Major US firms like Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have set up offices in the business-friendly country, alongside Chinese companies like TikTok-owner ByteDance and Tencent. But Singapore's openness to business has also made it the ideal address to place orders for restricted advanced semiconductors. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the chip giant earns. But notably, only 2% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, which acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. While Singapore does not necessarily prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls. Advanced semiconductors, crucial for the development of AI models, are at the centre of the US and China's technological rivalry. US officials have long viewed the country's technological supremacy as a matter of national security and have expressed concerns that sharing the best chips could give China's economy and military a boost. Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair. Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said. The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump. 'A handshake with Jensen' Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation. "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost." Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question." But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine". Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm. Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading. In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang". Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation. For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday. - Published1 day ago

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang". Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation. For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday. - Published1 day ago

news.title: Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive'
news.summary: Pakistan's ex-prime minister, who has been in prison since August 2023, says he has been denied justice.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive'
news.summaryTr: Pakistan's ex-prime minister, who has been in prison since August 2023, says he has been denied justice.
news.articleText: Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive' - Published Pakistan's jailed former PM Imran Khan has appealed for urgent medical treatment, saying that his and his wife's health has been deteriorating. "At 74, this unrelenting state is taking me to a place from which I may not return alive," the cricket star-turned-politician wrote in a letter published by his lawyer Salman Safdar. Authorities in Islamabad maintain that Khan gets seen weekly by doctors, who have assessed that he is of "satisfactory" health. Khan, who faces more than 100 charges, has been in prison since August 2023. His wife Bushra Bibi was jailed along with him last year. Khan argues the cases against them, ranging from corruption to selling state gifts, are politically motivated. Concerns over Khan's health have grown louder in the past year, with his family claiming he has lost most of his vision in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action. In his letter, Khan wrote that doctors have told him he is "highly vulnerable to a brain haemorrhage and cardiac arrest", and that his heart has already "suffered damage". He also expressed concern for Bushra Bibi, whom he says suffered a detached retina in April and underwent surgery in secrecy. Khan said he fears she may lose her sight without further surgery. "I have fought impossible legal battles in countless cases, and I have not stopped. But the system has stopped giving me justice," he wrote. He said that he is being held in solitary confinement for up to 22 hours a day, where he is allowed neither visits by his family nor access to books and television, and that this has "taken a heavy toll" on his mental health. He also claimed he had only seen his lawyers four times over the past year. "I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive," he wrote. Pakistan's parliamentary affairs minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry disputed these claims, saying Khan is "provided with all facilities in prison, including food of his own choosing". "[He] is currently the most well-accommodated prisoner in Pakistan," the minister told reporters. Authorities also say Khan was taken to a government-run hospital for an eye injection a week ago, where doctors deemed him "clinically stable". Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022. His arrest in May 2023 sparked large-scale, violent protests by supporters, who ransacked the corps commander's residence in Lahore, smashing chandeliers and making away with furniture, paintings, and even peacocks, among other things. At least eight people died in the protests and the army were called in to quell the violence. Even behind bars, Khan remains a force in Pakistani politics. Thousands of his supporters took to the streets in early October in a dayslong march, demanding his release. Authorities later ordered a crackdown on protests and imposed a state of emergency in Khan's party stronghold, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Former international cricket captains have made several appeals in recent months to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, insisting that Khan be given proper medical care.

items.titleTr: Crimea bridge shut after reported Ukrainian strike, as Russia hits Kyiv crossings
items.summaryTr: The bridge linking Crimea and Russia has reportedly sustained major damage, while two routes through Kyiv are closed.
items.articleText: Crimea bridge shut after reported Ukrainian strike, as Russia hits Kyiv crossings - Published A key bridge linking occupied Crimea and Russia is closed after reports a Ukrainian strike inflicted major damage, during a night in which the warring countries both targeted major crossings. A former adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky shared images purporting to show that a section of the Crimea bridge - also known as the Kerch Bridge - had collapsed into the water. Meanwhile, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern and Southern bridges, important routes over the Dnipro River, were closed after Russian ballistic missile strikes. Those attacks came a day after Ukraine began its most recent attempt to disable the Crimea bridge, a prized Kremlin asset seen as a symbol of Russia's occupation. Two people were killed in that strike overnight on Sunday, the Russian-installed governor of Crimea said. Former Ukrainian adviser Anton Gerashchenko shared images and video footage appearing to show extensive damage to the bridge from the latest strike, with a support arch and road section seen protruding from the water below. BBC News has not independently verified those images. The bridge, which has come under repeated attack by Ukrainian forces, was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014, and was personally opened by Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2018. While Ukraine has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the Crimea bridge is an attempt do increase the political cost on Putin. The severity of the latest strike on the route, which is protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences, is still not fully clear - but Russian state media reported a meeting was due to be held on Tuesday to discuss the situation. Crimea's Moscow-backed governor Sergei Aksyonov confirmed on Telegram that traffic over the bridge had been suspended. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between the Chinese, US and Russian leaders in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. Loud explosions were heard in Kyiv just before midnight on Tuesday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water. Some of Kyiv's above-ground subway services were damaged in the overnight attacks, officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Residents of Kyiv typically shelter in the city's underground stations during air raids. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. These latest Russian strikes will cause major disruption, with traffic already reportedly building in the capital. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the Cherkast region, according to local officials. The latest round of tit-for-tat strikes came after US, Ukrainian and European officials held talks on ways to facilitate "direct engagement" between Russia and Europe to end the war. Following Monday's meeting, US envoy Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law, said the US was committed to providing Ukraine with a "strong, credible security guarantees", as well as a path towards EU membership. He added that Nato "will remain a critical pillar of European security", and that preparations are underway for a further multilateral meeting "in the near future". Zelensky said that the meeting was "difficult", adding that more needed to be done to support Ukraine's defence against Russian ballistic missile strikes, which he said were being provided by North Korea. The Ukrainian president has long called for European nations to be included in any peace talks, which he argues is necessary because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the EU. Meanwhile, Ukrainian officials said the final death toll from a Russian attack on the southern Ukrainian village of Kamyshuvakha earlier this month had reached 72. Four people are still considered missing after the bombing, which Ukrainian officials said was one of the deadliest individual attacks since the start of the war in 2022. Footage, from a camera on one of the killed police officers, showed residents going to an underground shelter after the initial attack on 2 November. Soon after a blast is heard and flames are seen as the shelter is hit. Ukrainian police said of those killed were police officers, "staff of the gymnasium, utility workers and medical personnel". Russia's launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. items.articleText: JPMorgan'ın Türkiye hamlesi neyin sinyali? Uzman isim borsada 4 sektöre dikkat çekti - JPMorgan'ın Türkiye için tavsiyesini "ağırlık artır" seviyesine yükseltmesi, Borsa İstanbul'da yabancı yatırımcı beklentilerini yeniden gündeme taşıdı. Kuveyt Türk Yatırım Araştırma Direktörü Dr. Kutay Gözgör, yabancı ilgisinin yoğunlaşabileceği sektörleri ve endekste yükselişin kritik şartlarını açıkladı. Kuveyt Türk Yatırım Araştırma Direktörü Dr. Kutay Gözgör, CNBC-e ekranlarında Şafak Tükle'nin sunduğu Para Ekranı programında Borsa İstanbul'un teknik görünümünü, yabancı yatırımcı beklentilerini ve 2027 yılına ilişkin piyasa öngörülerini değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle JPMorgan'ın Türkiye için yatırım tavsiyesini "nötr" seviyesinden "ağırlık artır"a yükseltmesini önemli bir gelişme olarak nitelendiren Gözgör, Borsa İstanbul'daki iskontolu değerlemelerin yabancı yatırımcı açısından fırsat sunduğunu söyledi. Yabancı yatırımcı için ilk sinyaller Borsa İstanbul'da hem endeks hem de sektör bazında ucuz bir görünüm bulunduğunu belirten Gözgör, düşük değerlemelerin tek başına yükseliş için yeterli olmadığını vurguladı. Yabancı yatırımcıların önümüzdeki dönemde seçici hareket edeceğini ifade eden Gözgör, 2027 yılında ekonomik normalleşme süreci ve sermaye piyasalarına yönelik düzenlemelerle birlikte yabancı girişlerinin kademeli olarak artabileceğini söyledi. Gözgör, özellikle bankacılık, havacılık, perakende ve holding hisselerinin yabancı yatırımcıların odağında kalabileceğini, yükselişin piyasanın geneline yayılmasının ise zaman alacağını belirtti. Borsa İstanbul'da 12.500 puan kritik Endeksin teknik görünümünü de değerlendiren Gözgör, eylül ortasından itibaren yaşanan ve yaklaşık yüzde 30'a ulaşan düşüşün sona erme sinyalleri verdiğini söyledi. Borsa İstanbul'da bir taban oluşumu gözlemlediklerini belirten Gözgör, dönüş hareketinin teyit edilmesi için 12.500 puanın üzerinde kapanış gerektiğini vurguladı. Endeksin bu seviyeyi test edebileceğini ancak güçlü ve kesintisiz bir yükseliş için henüz yeterli ivmenin bulunmadığını ifade eden Gözgör, 12.500 puan sonrasında yatay bir hareketin görülebileceğini, ardından 14.000-15.000 puan bölgesinin gündeme gelebileceğini kaydetti. İşlem hacmindeki düşüşe dikkat çekti Yabancı yatırımcı girişlerinin hızlanması için piyasa likiditesinin iyileşmesi gerektiğini belirten Gözgör, işlem hacimlerindeki gerilemeye dikkat çekti. Eylül başında günlük 250-300 milyar liraya ulaşan işlem hacminin son dönemde ortalama 150-160 milyar liraya gerilediğini söyleyen Gözgör, bu durumun piyasadaki toparlanmayı sınırlayan unsurlardan biri olduğunu ifade etti. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek'in uluslararası yatırımcılarla gerçekleştireceği görüşmelerin de olumlu etkiler yaratabileceğini belirten Gözgör, şirketlerin iskontolu değerlemelerinin yatırımcı ilgisini artırma potansiyeli taşıdığını ancak bunun için likidite ve yatırım ortamındaki koşulların iyileşmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Gözgör, yabancı yatırımcıların Borsa İstanbul'daki ağırlıklarını artırmasını beklediğini ancak bu sürecin hızlı bir dönüşten ziyade seçici ve kademeli bir toparlanma şeklinde gerçekleşebileceğini sözlerine ekledi.

items.articleText: Mert Yılmaz açıkladı: Fon krizinin ardından yatırımcı rotasını nereye çevirebilir? İNFO Yatırım Müdür Yardımcısı Mert Yılmaz, yatırım fonlarında yaşanan gelişmelerin ardından yatırımcıların geleneksel yatırım araçlarına yönelebileceğini belirtti. Yılmaz, altın, döviz, gayrimenkul ve arsa yatırımlarının yeniden öne çıkabileceğini söyledi. İnfo Yatırım Menkul Değerler Müdür Yardımcısı Mert Yılmaz, CNBC-e'nin "Makro Gündem" programında Şafak Tükle'nin sorularını yanıtladı. Yılmaz, TCMB'nin aralık ayında faiz indirimine gitmesini beklediğini belirterek, enflasyon beklentileri ve politika faizi tahminlerine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu. TCMB'nin 2027 yılı enflasyon tahminini yüzde 15'ten yüzde 21'e yükselttiğini hatırlatan Yılmaz, piyasanın 12 ay sonrası enflasyon beklentisinin yüzde 24 seviyelerinde bulunduğunu kaydetti. Yılmaz, "Genel olarak 2026 yıl sonu enflasyonunun yüzde 24-25'lerde, 2027 yıl sonu politika faizinin ise yüzde 28-29'larda olması mümkün. Dolayısıyla belki çok istenilen hızda olmasa da bir faiz indirim döngüsü devam edecek." dedi. Söz konusu kısıtlamaların geçtiğimiz günlerde bir miktar esnetildiğini anımsatan Yılmaz, TCMB'nin bu alanda yeni bir değişikliğe gidip gitmeyeceğinin izlenmesi gerektiğini ifade etti. "Kredi faizlerinin düşmesi konut fiyatlarını yukarı taşıyor" Konut piyasasına ilişkin değerlendirmelerde de bulunan Yılmaz, kredi faizlerinin düşmeye başladığı veya düşüş beklentisinin güçlendiği dönemlerde konut fiyatlarının da yükseldiğine dikkati çekti. Konut veya iş yeri satın almak isteyenlerin kredi faizlerinin düşmesini beklediğini belirten Yılmaz, bu süreçte kredi maliyetlerindeki düşüşten elde edilecek tasarrufun üzerinde bir fiyat artışıyla karşılaşılabildiğini kaydetti. 'Geleneksel yatırım araçlarına yönelim güçlenebilir' Yatırım fonlarında yaşanan gelişmelerin ardından yatırımcı davranışlarının nasıl şekilleneceğinin önem taşıdığını belirten Yılmaz, finansal piyasalarda ciddi bir güven sorunu bulunduğunu ve bunun kısa sürede aşılmasının gerçekçi olmadığını söyledi. Yılmaz, fonlarda parasına erişemeyen ve nakit ihtiyacı bulunan bazı yatırımcıların evlerini ve araçlarını satmayı beklediğini, diğer bir grubun ise fiyatların düşmesini veya fonlardaki parasına yeniden erişebilmeyi beklediğini anlattı. Nitelikli yatırımcı kriterinin 10 milyon liradan 50 milyon liraya çıkarılması halinde serbest fon piyasasının neredeyse ortadan kalkabileceğine işaret eden Yılmaz, sorunun serbest fonlardan mı yoksa bu fonların denetim mekanizmasından mı kaynaklandığının doğru tespit edilmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Yılmaz, "Sadece bir yeri, bir parametreyi, bir ürünü günah keçisi seçmek ve orayı bitirmek yerine, bu işin masanın bir tarafındaki kanun koyucu, düzenleyici, bürokrat ve teknokratlarla diğer tarafındaki insanların bir araya gelip görüş alışverişinde bulunması lazım." dedi. Seçimlerin 2028'in mart veya nisan ayında yapılmasının öngörüldüğünü hatırlatan Yılmaz, yıl sonunda açıklanacak asgari ücret ve emekli maaşı zamlarının piyasalar tarafından nasıl algılanacağının önemli olduğunu belirtti. Söz konusu artışların 2027 sonunda seçim mesajı olarak değerlendirilmesi halinde ekonomik görünümün değişebileceğine işaret eden Yılmaz, böyle bir senaryonun daha hızlı faiz indirimlerini, kredi faizlerinde daha belirgin düşüşleri ve para politikasında gevşemeyi beraberinde getirebileceğini söyledi. Yılmaz, bu gelişmelerin ekonomik aktiviteyi canlandırarak özellikle borsa başta olmak üzere piyasalarda olumlu fiyatlamalara zemin hazırlayabileceğini belirterek, seçim öncesindeki olası olumlu tablonun seçim sonrasında yeniden enflasyon riski yaratabileceğinin de göz ardı edilmemesi gerektiğini sözlerine ekledi.

items.titleTr: Which areas have the most jobs for 16-24 year-olds? Use our look-up to find out
items.summaryTr: How many jobs are there where you live and in which sectors are you most likely to find an opening?
items.articleText: Which areas have the most jobs for 16-24 year-olds? Use our look-up to find out - Published If you're one of the nearly one million people aged 16-24 not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet" - then you might be wondering where to start. Under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work, a major review aimed at cutting the number of Neets will say. But how many jobs are there where you live and in which sectors are you most likely to find an opening? How many job vacancies are there? There is no official measure of how many vacancies are suitable for young people, but across the whole economy there were 690,000 jobs available in the August to October period this year, which is the lowest number since early 2021. The Covid pandemic led to huge swings in the number of job vacancies available as companies reacted to shutdowns and then reopened as restrictions were lifted. Stripping out the fluctuations seen during the pandemic, the number of vacancies is now at its lowest level for 12 years. Apprenticeships have often been a way for people to get their first taste of employment. In England the number of people starting apprenticeships has risen in recent years, although this has been driven by an increase in those aged 25 and over after schemes for older workers were fully rolled out in 2008. The number of people aged 24 and under starting apprenticeships in England in 2025 was 172,230, down from a peak of 291,300 in 2012. Where are the available jobs? Where you live will often have a big impact on your ability to find a job. We have used online job adverts to help identify the number of vacancies suitable for young people in the area they live, relative to the size of the local population. The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank used AI to help identify the jobs, which were broadly defined as roles requiring relatively low experience or education. According to its analysis, South Oxfordshire had 387 suitable vacancies per 1,000 18 to 24-year-olds in the area - the most of any local authority. Rotherham had the least, at 53 per 1,000. Use this tool to check out the situation in your area. The data for London is only available for the region as a whole and is not broken down by individual councils. Which sectors have the most entry-level jobs? Even if there are jobs available in your area, you might not find one in the sector you want to work in. The sector with the highest average number of entry-level vacancies in the year to October was teaching, with most of those jobs being for teaching assistants, learning support and cover supervisor roles, according to jobs website Adzuna. The next largest was hospitality and catering, traditionally an area where younger people get their first experience of work. Adzuna, a major online jobs website, includes adverts for full-time roles marked as entry-level, those asking for up to two years' experience, graduate roles, internships and apprenticeships. Accounting and finance had the third-highest number of job openings. What are the typical rates of pay? Figures on salaries for vacancies can be patchy because many employers do not include them in job adverts. Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently urged businesses to start publishing salaries ahead of plans to make pay details compulsory in adverts. Only about 40% of Adzuna's jobs data for the year to October stated a salary, although that figure varies widely by sector. Here are the average salaries for jobs in the sectors with the largest number of entry-level jobs, according to Adzuna. The highest average salary is £30,530 in engineering, while social care has the lowest at £25,880.

items.summaryTr: TMSF'nin Form Sünger'in satışına ilişkin ihale ilanı Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı. Şirket için muhammen bedel 5 milyar 250 milyon lira olarak belirlenirken açık artırma 5 Ocak 2027'de yapılacak.
items.articleText: TMSF, Form Sünger'i 5,25 milyar liraya satışa çıkarıyor YAYIN TARİHİ, 17 Kasım 2026 10:14 PAYLAŞ - TMSF'nin Form Sünger'in satışına ilişkin ihale ilanı Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı. Şirket için muhammen bedel 5 milyar 250 milyon lira olarak belirlenirken açık artırma 5 Ocak 2027'de yapılacak. TMSF'nin Form Sünger'in satışına ilişkin ihale ilanı, Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İhalede muhammen bedel 5 milyar 250 milyon lira, katılım teminatı 270 milyon lira, şartname ücreti 300 bin lira, veri inceleme ve tesis ziyaret ücreti ise 1 milyon lira olarak belirlendi. İhaleye katılabilmek için 4 Ocak 2027 saat 16.30'a kadar kapalı zarf içinde teklif verilmesi gerekiyor. Söz konusu ihaleye ilişkin açık artırma ise 5 Ocak 2027 saat 10.00'da TMSF'nin İstanbul Esentepe'deki binasında gerçekleştirilecek. Kaynak: AA

items.articleText: Borsada KAP hareketliliği: Milyonluk anlaşmalar, temettü ve kapasite artışı Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören şirketlerden milyonlarca liralık yeni iş anlaşmaları, yatırım ve kapasite artışı açıklamaları geldi. Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yapılan bildirimlerde yeni sözleşmeler ve temettü kararları öne çıktı. DCT Trading (DCTTR), 2026-2027 sezonu yurt içi pamuk alımları kapsamında 90,2 milyon TL tutarında anlaşma imzaladı. Şirket, söz konusu anlaşmanın yeni sezon pamuk tedariki kapsamında gerçekleştirildiğini açıkladı. Ekos Teknoloji (EKOS), yurt içi ve yurt dışındaki firmalarla toplam 434,2 milyon TL tutarında elektrik ekipmanları satış sözleşmeleri imzaladı. Şirket, ürünlerin teslimatını 2026'nın kalan döneminde ve 2027'nin ilk yarısında tamamlamayı planlıyor. Gıpta Ofis (GIPTA) pay başına brüt 0,0077651 TL temettü dağıtırken, hissenin teorik fiyatı 30,172 TL olarak belirlendi. Göknur Gıda (GOKNR), Afyonkarahisar'ın Dinar ilçesindeki 6.840 metrekarelik ilave soğuk hava deposu yatırımını tamamlayarak işletmeye aldı. Yatırımla birlikte şirketin meyve depolama kapasitesi 2 bin tondan 15 bin tona yükseldi.

items.articleText: Konut satışları ekimde yüzde 23,3 azaldı - TÜİK verilerine göre Türkiye genelinde konut satışları, 2026 yılı ekim ayında geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 23,3 düşerek 131 bin 72 oldu. İlk el konut satışları yüzde 13,1, ikinci el satışlar yüzde 28,5 geriledi. Yabancılara yapılan satışlar ise yüzde 0,9 artışla 2 bin 259'a çıktı. Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu (TÜİK) verilerine göre, Türkiye genelinde konut satışları ekim ayında bir önceki yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 23,3 azalarak 131 bin 072 oldu. Ocak-ekim döneminde ise konut satışları bir önceki yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 9,2 azalışla 1 milyon 223 bin 991 olarak gerçekleşti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Ekim ayında ilk el konut satışları bir önceki yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 13,1 azalarak 50 bin 105, ikinci el konut satışları yüzde 28,5 azalarak 80 bin 967 oldu. Toplam konut satışları içinde ilk el satışların payı yüzde 38,2, ikinci el satışların payı yüzde 61,8 olarak kaydedildi. Ocak-ekim döneminde ilk el konut satışları yüzde 2,4 azalışla 410 bin 018, ikinci el konut satışları yüzde 12,3 azalışla 813 bin 973 oldu. İpotekli konut satışları ekim ayında bir önceki yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 5,7 azalarak 23 bin 286 olurken diğer konut satışları yüzde 26,3 azalışla 107 bin 786 olarak gerçekleşti. Toplam konut satışları içinde ipotekli satışların payı yüzde 17,8, diğer satışların payı yüzde 82,2 oldu. Ocak-ekim döneminde ipotekli konut satışları yüzde 20,8 artarak 235 bin 496'ya yükselirken diğer satışlar yüzde 14,3 azalarak 988 bin 495 oldu. Takvim etkilerinden arındırılmış serilerde, bir önceki yılın aynı ayına göre ilk el konut satışları yüzde 7,4, ikinci el konut satışları yüzde 24,0 azaldı. Mevsim ve takvim etkilerinden arındırılmış serilerde ise bir önceki aya göre ilk el konut satışları yüzde 4,8, ikinci el konut satışları yüzde 1,4 azaldı. Yabancılara yapılan konut satışları ekim ayında bir önceki yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 0,9 artarak 2 bin 259 oldu. Toplam konut satışları içinde yabancılara yapılan satışların payı yüzde 1,7 olarak gerçekleşti. Ocak-ekim döneminde yabancılara yapılan konut satışları bir önceki yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 3,6 azalarak 17 bin 567 oldu. Ekim ayında ülke uyruklarına göre en fazla konut satışı sırasıyla 477 ile Rusya Federasyonu, 193 ile İran ve 159 ile Irak vatandaşlarına yapıldı. İş yeri satışları ise ekim ayında bir önceki yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 12,6 azalarak 16 bin 489 oldu. İlk el iş yeri satışları yüzde 4,5 artışla 5 bin 519 olurken ikinci el iş yeri satışları yüzde 19,2 azalışla 10 bin 970 olarak gerçekleşti. İpotekli iş yeri satışları yüzde 37,4 artarak 724'e yükselirken diğer iş yeri satışları yüzde 14,0 azalarak 15 bin 765 oldu. Ocak-ekim döneminde iş yeri satışları bir önceki yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 6,0 azalarak 152 bin 032 olarak gerçekleşti. Bu dönemde ilk el iş yeri satışları yüzde 4,2 artışla 46 bin 151, ipotekli iş yeri satışları yüzde 58,8 artışla 6 bin 759 oldu. Takvim etkilerinden arındırılmış serilerde, bir önceki yılın aynı ayına göre ilk el iş yeri satışları yüzde 11,3 artarken ikinci el iş yeri satışları yüzde 14,3 azaldı. Mevsim ve takvim etkilerinden arındırılmış serilerde ise bir önceki aya göre ilk el iş yeri satışları yüzde 1,8, ikinci el iş yeri satışları yüzde 1,1 azaldı.

items.articleText: TÜİK açıkladı: Tarım-ÜFE ekimde yıllık yüzde 9,69 arttı - Tarım-ÜFE, ekimde aylık yüzde 1,02, yıllık yüzde 9,69 arttı. Yıllık ve aylık bazda en yüksek fiyat düşüşü ise turunçgillerde kaydedildi. Tarım ürünleri üretici fiyat endeksi (Tarım-ÜFE), ekim ayında bir önceki aya göre yüzde 1,02, geçen yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 9,69 yükseldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu (TÜİK), Ekim 2026 dönemine ilişkin Tarım-ÜFE verilerini açıkladı. Buna göre Tarım-ÜFE, ekimde bir önceki aya kıyasla yüzde 1,02, geçen yılın aralık ayına göre yüzde 8,12, geçen yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 9,69 ve 12 aylık ortalamalara göre yüzde 27,64 arttı. Sektörler incelendiğinde, ekimde bir önceki aya göre tarım ve avcılık ürünleri ile ilgili hizmetlerde yüzde 1,13 artış kaydedildi. Ormancılık ürünleri ve ilgili hizmetlerde yüzde 0,37, balık ve diğer balıkçılık ürünleri ile su ürünlerinde yüzde 0,75 azalış gerçekleşti. Ana gruplarda ise tek yıllık bitkisel ürünlerde yüzde 7,94, canlı hayvanlar ve hayvansal ürünlerde yüzde 0,91 artış görülürken çok yıllık bitkisel ürünlerde yüzde 7,13 düşüş kaydedildi. Yıllık ve aylık değişimde turunçgiller öne çıktı Yıllık değişimin en yüksek olduğu alt grup, yüzde 57,83 azalışla turunçgiller oldu. Aylık bazda da en yüksek düşüş yüzde 27,67 ile yine turunçgillerde gerçekleşti.

items.title: Ex-Robinhood engineer pleads guilty to $125K Hyperliquid trading scheme
items.summary: The former Robinhood engineer used confidential information about upcoming Robinhood token listings to trade on Hyperliquid.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Ex-Robinhood engineer pleads guilty to $125K Hyperliquid trading scheme
items.summaryTr: The former Robinhood engineer used confidential information about upcoming Robinhood token listings to trade on Hyperliquid.
items.articleText: Ex-Robinhood engineer pleads guilty to $125K Hyperliquid trading scheme The former Robinhood engineer used confidential information about upcoming Robinhood token listings to trade on Hyperliquid. Former Robinhood software engineer Huaisong “Jerry” Xiang has pleaded guilty to wire fraud after using confidential information about upcoming crypto listings on the platform to trade perpetual futures on the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, earning $125,523 in illicit profits. On Monday, the US Department of Justice said that Xiang entered the plea before US District Judge Colleen McMahon and agreed to forfeit $125,523. Xiang faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison and is scheduled to be sentenced on Feb. 25, 2027. Prosecutors said the software engineer had access to nonpublic information about which tokens Robinhood Crypto planned to list and when. Between 2025 and 2026, he repeatedly bought perpetual futures tied to those tokens before the announcements were made public. The plea follows September charges against Xiang and another former Robinhood engineer, Hefu Chai. Both were accused of exploiting internal listing information to trade on Hyperliquid, with prosecutors initially alleging that each made over $50,000. The DOJ’s Monday announcement did not provide an update on Chai’s case. In May, crypto analytics firm Kaiko flagged suspicious Hyperliquid trading ahead of Robinhood’s Jan. 15 listing of Lighter (LIT). One of the wallets identified in its investigation matches an address that prosecutors later linked to Chai, who allegedly used it to trade LIT perpetuals ahead of the listing. Related: Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’

items.title: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72
items.summary: Efforts to recover bodies after a “double-tap” attack in southern Ukraine are being hampered by continuing Russian strikes, officials say.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72
items.summaryTr: Efforts to recover bodies after a “double-tap” attack in southern Ukraine are being hampered by continuing Russian strikes, officials say.
items.articleText: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72 - Published Ukrainian officials have accused Russia of targeting rescue and recovery operations two weeks after a deadly "double-tap" strike at a village close to the front line killed at least 72 people. Ukraine says Russia carried out two attacks in succession on a humanitarian aid centre in the village of Komyshuvakha on 2 November - including the use of what it said was a 3,000kg (6,600lb) aerial bomb on a shelter where residents had fled for safety. Verified images posted in the days after the attack show damage to emergency vehicles and excavation equipment at the site. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) told BBC Verify there have been multiple Russian strikes during the rescue. The DSNS said three police officers, four workers and two rescue dogs were injured while five vehicles were damaged. "Due to the threat of repeated shelling, emergency workers are constantly forced to periodically suspend work and retreat to a safe place," it added. The DSNS said the death toll had risen to at least 72 people making it one of the deadliest single incidents since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Oleksiy, an intelligence officer investigating the incident for Ukraine's SBU security service, who asked to be identified only by his first name, said rescue vehicles were "clearly marked" and accused Russia of "deliberately destroying humanitarian equipment". He added the village's infrastructure and the people still living in Komyshuvakha are also being systematically targeted by drones and bombs. Oleksiy accused Russian forces of "outright terror against civilians, against peaceful residents" to make life on the front line impossible. BBC Verify has confirmed videos being shared by Ukrainian police that show rescue workers at the scene shouting "drone, drone" and running for cover on the day after the 2 November attack. A group can also be seen treating a victim. Bodies are still to be recovered from the rubble, Oleksiy said. "The enemy knows perfectly well that what is being carried out there is essentially a humanitarian operation to search for the dead." BBC Verify has asked the Russian Ministry of Defence for comment specifically about the Komyshuvakha attacks but has not received a response. A general statement released on 2 November by the Russian MoD said it had targeted energy and transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian military across the country. While there are no military or industrial facilities in Komyshuvakha it is close to a key route used for Ukrainian troop movements, supplies and evacuations. The village was previously reported to have been struck by the Russians on 28 October. Fears of second strike heard on police radios Local people headed to the shelter area on 2 November after being told by a local Telegram group that aid would be distributed between 10:00 and 12:00 local time (08:00-10:00 GMT). Ukrainian authorities said an initial strike, at 09:45 local time, hit buildings above ground killing one woman. Bodycam footage, released by Ukrainian police in edited segments and analysed by BBC Verify, shows people trying to free a casualty from the rubble before declaring she had died. Throughout the footage, warnings of an impending second strike can be heard on police radios with increasing urgency until people are instructed to run to the underground shelter. The same footage, which was taken around an hour after the first attack, goes on to show people in a shelter. As they wait in silence a large explosion can be heard and the video goes dark. Aftermath video filmed later shows bodies being recovered from a large crater immediately above the shelter. Twisted iron and rubble from the structure below can be seen beneath the surface. Funerals have been held almost daily for the victims of the attack, including locals working to administer aid distribution, those seeking to collect it and soldiers who officials say arrived to assist with rescue efforts. Trevor Ball, bomb disposal expert at intelligence firm at Armament Research Services, said a crater seen in the footage was consistent with the damage and depth left by a FAB-3000, a 3,000kg Russian bomb which can destroy underground structures. His comments were echoed by Chris Proops, an ex-UK National Crime Agency investigator, who said the scale of the damage at the scene matched the size of the FAB-3000. Ball and Proops both confirmed verified photos of munition fragments obtained by BBC Verify from Ukrainian authorities show part of a guidance kit that is compatible with the FAB-3000, which increases the weapon's accuracy and allows it to be fired from a greater distance from the target. International law experts told BBC Verify that Russia had committed a war crime if it knowingly attacked rescue workers. Ben Saul, professor of international law at the University of Sydney, said this "appears to be either a deliberate attack on civilians or civilian objects - a war crime - or an indiscriminate attack - also a war crime". Prof Samuel Moyn of Yale University said "directly targeting rescuers or their equipment is a gross violation of international humanitarian law". Precautions have to be taken to ensure that strikes target combatants rather than others, he added. Additional reporting by Margaryta Maliukova, BBC Monitoring

items.title: Vance says he will decide 'sometime next year' about 2028 US presidential run
items.summary: The US vice-president tells Fox News that when he makes a decision to run or otherwise, he will "be all in on whatever that decision is".

items.titleTr: Vance says he will decide 'sometime next year' about 2028 US presidential run
items.summaryTr: The US vice-president tells Fox News that when he makes a decision to run or otherwise, he will "be all in on whatever that decision is".
items.articleText: Vance says he will decide 'sometime next year' about 2028 US presidential run - Published US Vice-President JD Vance has said he will make a decision "sometime next year" about whether or not he will run for president in 2028. In an interview with Fox News, Vance would not provide a timeline on making a determination, but signaled he is not in a hurry to make up his mind. "I haven't made a decision. We'll figure it out sometime next year," Vance said. When pressed by host Laura Ingraham, he added: "When I make a decision, I'll be all in on whatever that decision is." The comments came amid growing interest in Vance's next moves in the weeks since voters handed both President Donald Trump and Republicans a resounding defeat in the midterm elections. People in Vance's orbit who have spoken to the BBC said the November elections did not change the timeline around his decision-making process for 2028. He is expected to run but allies believe he could wait several months to make a final decision. Speculation about Vance's White House aspirations began the moment President Trump selected him as his 2024 running mate. The pick positioned Vance, who entered the White House as one of the youngest vice-presidents in US history, as the most likely heir to Trump's Make America Great Again (Maga) movement. But while serving in office, Vance has carefully avoided discussing his own political ambitions. He kept that up during the midterms, when supporters frequently interrupted his campaign speeches to urge him to run in 2028. Vance's stock response was that Republicans needed to focus on the election at hand in November. But with the midterms in the rearview mirror, and Republicans eager to move on from their 2026 drubbing, the next election at hand is now the 2028 presidential race. - Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war - Published5 November - The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now? - Published8 November Vance would likely jump to the top of the Republican primary field whenever he launches his bid, should he choose to run. But the contest is expected to be a competitive process with a large field of candidates. Numerous other high-profile Republicans are rumoured to be interested in running or have said publicly that they are mulling a White House bid. The list includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, outgoing Florida Governor and 2024 hopeful Ron DeSantis, and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie, among others. Trump has praised Vance and Rubio on several occasions, while also insisting that he is not sure who he will endorse in 2028 - or if he will weigh in at all. The president's endorsement would be influential with the Maga base. But the midterms revealed widespread frustration with many of his second-term policies, complicating the path forward for potential candidates like Vance who are tied to Trump's agenda. Vance blamed the midterm results on the war with Iran in a post-election social media post. In it, he also mapped out a plan for winning back Republican voters, which included ending the war and focusing on the economy. The message was widely seen as a first step by Vance to distance himself from Trump ahead of a 2028 run. In the Fox News interview, Vance reiterated his view that the war came with a "political cost", but said it has not damaged his relationship with Trump. "There's no daylight" on the Iran war between Trump and senior administration officials including himself, Vance said. He added that Trump would not let the conflict become a "forever war" and said the administration would not let the war, which was launched by the US and Israel in February 2026, even become "a two-year commitment". Vance also discussed the nationwide air traffic outrage last week, which brought air travel across the US to a standstill for several hours. The vice-president called on lawmakers to fix the issue in the final weeks of the current congressional session. He also touched on the scandal engulfing Nvidia, its former CEO Jensen Huang and its implications for US-China relations. Vance said there was still no "clarity" about the accuracy of reports that a woman with whom Huang reportedly had an affair with was indeed a Chinese spy. "There is a lack of clarity about it. I don't know and [Trump] doesn't know whether this woman was a spy or not," Vance said. Related topics - Published6 November - Published7 November - Published4 November

items.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss
items.summary: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss
items.summaryTr: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
items.articleText: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss - Published Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for the company's co-founder Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, supported the effort. Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, joining a list of supporters including SpaceX's Elon Musk who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign. But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in reinstating him after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy. The same day, the White House also said it will further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia. The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. Since Huang's departure, more than 175,000 people have signed an open letter calling for the board to reinstate the tech billionaire while an ongoing internal probe is conducted. Major tech bosses, including Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return. The "Stand with Jensen" campaign claims to have been launched by current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, all demanding the return of the former chief executive. They expressed concerns the firm's co-founder "was removed without meaningful due process". Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back. Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of the affair but resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him. The scandal-hit tech boss was discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times, external, though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him. A representative for Huang declined to comment on the report. The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House. Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal erupted, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy". Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company. The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions. New rules The Trump administration on Monday also issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres, which have been allegedly used as a way for Chinese firms to gain access to advanced chips to train AI models. The move comes ahead of a meeting this week between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, whose countries are locked in a race to lead AI development. The interim rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to prevent them from being illegally diverted to China. The measure is designed to ensure existing restrictions on sensitive US technology "cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the Department of Commerce said. Huang has been a vocal advocate for easing chip export restrictions on China, arguing that broad access to global markets is crucial for the competitiveness of the US. He said in 2025 that the market for AI chips in China would eventually reach $50bn - a sum Huang said "is like Boeing - not a plane - the entire company". In 2025, Nvidia won an approval to sell some advanced AI chips in China after Huang's repeated lobbying efforts in Washington. - How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security? - Published4 days ago - How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House - Published3 days ago The ex-Nvidia boss' affair with Alice Huang, the former director of a Singaporean data centre firm called Megaspeed, has raised the level of scrutiny over deals abroad. The small South East Asian business hub has been a draw for companies all around the world, many of which have set up headquarters in Singapore. Major US firms like Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have set up offices in the business-friendly country, alongside Chinese companies like TikTok-owner ByteDance and Tencent. But Singapore's openness to business has also made it the ideal address to place orders for restricted advanced semiconductors. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the chip giant earns. But notably, only 2% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, which acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. While Singapore does not necessarily prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls. Advanced semiconductors, crucial for the development of AI models, are at the centre of the US and China's technological rivalry. US officials have long viewed the country's technological supremacy as a matter of national security and have expressed concerns that sharing the best chips could give China's economy and military a boost. Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair. Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said. The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump. 'A handshake with Jensen' Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation. "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost." Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question." But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine". Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm. Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading. In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang". Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation. For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday. - Published1 day ago

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang". Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation. For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday. - Published1 day ago

items.title: Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive'
items.summary: Pakistan's ex-prime minister, who has been in prison since August 2023, says he has been denied justice.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive'
items.summaryTr: Pakistan's ex-prime minister, who has been in prison since August 2023, says he has been denied justice.
items.articleText: Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive' - Published Pakistan's jailed former PM Imran Khan has appealed for urgent medical treatment, saying that his and his wife's health has been deteriorating. "At 74, this unrelenting state is taking me to a place from which I may not return alive," the cricket star-turned-politician wrote in a letter published by his lawyer Salman Safdar. Authorities in Islamabad maintain that Khan gets seen weekly by doctors, who have assessed that he is of "satisfactory" health. Khan, who faces more than 100 charges, has been in prison since August 2023. His wife Bushra Bibi was jailed along with him last year. Khan argues the cases against them, ranging from corruption to selling state gifts, are politically motivated. Concerns over Khan's health have grown louder in the past year, with his family claiming he has lost most of his vision in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action. In his letter, Khan wrote that doctors have told him he is "highly vulnerable to a brain haemorrhage and cardiac arrest", and that his heart has already "suffered damage". He also expressed concern for Bushra Bibi, whom he says suffered a detached retina in April and underwent surgery in secrecy. Khan said he fears she may lose her sight without further surgery. "I have fought impossible legal battles in countless cases, and I have not stopped. But the system has stopped giving me justice," he wrote. He said that he is being held in solitary confinement for up to 22 hours a day, where he is allowed neither visits by his family nor access to books and television, and that this has "taken a heavy toll" on his mental health. He also claimed he had only seen his lawyers four times over the past year. "I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive," he wrote. Pakistan's parliamentary affairs minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry disputed these claims, saying Khan is "provided with all facilities in prison, including food of his own choosing". "[He] is currently the most well-accommodated prisoner in Pakistan," the minister told reporters. Authorities also say Khan was taken to a government-run hospital for an eye injection a week ago, where doctors deemed him "clinically stable". Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022. His arrest in May 2023 sparked large-scale, violent protests by supporters, who ransacked the corps commander's residence in Lahore, smashing chandeliers and making away with furniture, paintings, and even peacocks, among other things. At least eight people died in the protests and the army were called in to quell the violence. Even behind bars, Khan remains a force in Pakistani politics. Thousands of his supporters took to the streets in early October in a dayslong march, demanding his release. Authorities later ordered a crackdown on protests and imposed a state of emergency in Khan's party stronghold, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Former international cricket captains have made several appeals in recent months to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, insisting that Khan be given proper medical care.
